explanation: When two tones of nearly equal frequency overlap, superposition makes their sum swell and fade: the loudness throbs at the beat frequency f_beat = |f1 - f2|. The product-to-sum identity rewrites the sum as a fast carrier at the average frequency (f1+f2)/2 multiplied by a slow envelope cos(2*pi*(df/2)*t); because loudness peaks at both the positive and negative humps of that envelope, the audible beat rate is the full |f1-f2|, not half of it. Musicians use this to tune — a slowing beat means the two pitches are converging. On the AP exam you compute f_beat from two given frequencies and identify the violet envelope as the modulation, not a separate wave.
bullets: Blue curve is the literal sum of the two sine tones (superposition).
Violet dashed curve is the +/- 2cos(2*pi*(df/2)*t) amplitude envelope.
One full loud-soft cycle per 1/|f1-f2| seconds = the beat period.
Smaller df -> slower throb -> the tones are closer to in tune.
